1.explanation:
All three files participate in how Lighthouse captures and simulates the page load under throttlingMethod=simulate. 

• driver.js implements gotoURL and trace recording lifecycles (waitForLoad, network-quiet, CPU-quiet) and determines when to stop capturing DevTools events. In simulate mode the trace is ended on the real loadEventFired, too early to catch late shifts.

• gather-runner.js orchestrates the passes and invokes driver.gotoURL with the default waitForLoad/idle settings. It doesn’t special-case simulate throttling to extend the capture window for LayoutShift events.

• load-simulator.js only computes the offline network/CPU slowdown parameters but has no hook for extending the simulation or trace capture to include later layout shifts. Fixing CLS under simulate will require updating these files so that when throttlingMethod=simulate Lighthouse holds the trace open (or waits for CPU idle) long enough to observe all late layout‐shift activity.
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse in “simulate” throttling mode (the Lantern‐based simulator), Lighthouse gathers an unthrottled trace of the page (including FCP and loadEventFired) and then stops capturing DevTools trace events as soon as the simulator believes the page load is complete. On pages like the PWA Venia bottoms page, additional images and overlays continue loading and shifting layout after the load event. Because the DevTools trace is cut off too early, no LayoutShift events are recorded and Cumulative Layout Shift reports as 0 (see screenshot), even though the live page exhibits significant late‐arriving shifts.
